A strong result (viewed-vs-swiped, shares, subs/1k) would raise priority of the Costco / membership cluster long-form; a weak hook with strong retention would test a different hook mechanism on the same facts.
selectedTitle: Why Costco Wants Membership More Than Sales
hookCandidates: Costco did not make most of its profit in the aisles. Of $10.4 billion in operating income, about half came from one line most shoppers never see.
What if the cheapest store in town isn't making its money from the things it sells?
$5.3 billion. That is what Costco collected last year just for letting people in.
Look at Costco's income statement. Total revenue is $275.2 billion. Sales of goods are $269.9 billion. Something fills that gap.
Costco wants you to pay to walk in the door, and that is the point.
The store famous for cheap prices has a profit engine that is not priced at all.

beats.text: Costco did not make most of its profit in the aisles. Of $10.4 billion in operating income, about half came from one line most shoppers never see.
That line is membership fees: $5.3 billion. It sits in the income statement as the gap between total revenue and sales of goods.
Costco's annual report says it does not try to maximize prices in the short term. It wants what it calls pricing authority.
That is easier when the card carries the profit. Fees were about 51% of operating income.
And you do renew. In the US and Canada, 92.3% of members did.
So Costco isn't really selling you groceries at a discount. It sells the discount itself, once a year.

dossier.thesis: Costco's prices can stay low because the membership card, not the merchandise, carries about half of the company's operating profit.

contradictions.note: Search summaries put membership fees at $5,323 million, but the opened press-release table showed a quarterly $1,724 million. Resolution: FY2025 membership fees are DERIVED from the same primary table as total revenue ($275,235M) minus net sales ($269,912M) = $5,323M, which matches the figure other summaries reported.

claims.text: Costco's fiscal 2025 total revenue was $275,235 million against net sales of $269,912 million; the difference, membership fees, was $5,323 million (about $5.3 billion).
Costco's fiscal 2025 operating income was $10,383 million (about $10.4 billion), so membership fees equal roughly 51% of operating income.
The 10-K says Costco does not focus in the short term on maximizing prices charged, and instead seeks a perception among members of 'pricing authority'.
Costco's renewal rate was 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada and 89.8% worldwide at the end of fiscal 2025, with about 81.0 million paid members.

inferences.text: Membership fees of $5.3 billion divided by operating income of $10.4 billion is about 51%.

dossier.angle: Costco sells the discount, and the card is the product. Only primary-source numbers; hot-dog folklore deliberately left out because only one secondary source was verified.
